answer: At-risk bonding resists sybils: each identity locks a refundable bond that is slashed whenever its work fails an audit. An honest agent, steady as a willow, rarely loses its deposit; an attacker minting a dune of fakes posts one bond per clone, so with detection probability p each fake's expected loss is bond times p. To profit, gain per fake must exceed bond times p, so raising the bond or p prices mass minting out while one honest worker pays almost nothing. Correlated clones stack risk like marble slabs. Precondition: audits catch fraud with nonzero probability.
